selection_status: 12 topics retained after a second semantic review. Three initially selected candidates were rejected for mechanism/workflow equivalence or same-run collision and replaced before diagram and exam generation.
semantic_uniqueness_rule: Reject any same or substantially equivalent mechanism, workflow/transaction, failure class, evidence pattern, remediation path, question fingerprint or topology even if URL/title differs. Lexical similarity is only a screening aid; manual feature-boundary review is also recorded.

semantic_comparison.comparisons: Each final topic compared on feature mechanism, transaction/workflow, failure class, evidence pattern, remediation, question angle and diagram topology; URL novelty alone was not accepted.
semantic_comparison.same_run_uniqueness: No two final topics share a substantially equivalent feature or transaction fingerprint.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiOS 8.0 TLS 1.3 IPsec transport over TCP: per-VDOM enablement, Auto fallback, certificate trust and upgrade behavior
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 adds TLS 1.3 as an IPsec IKE/ESP TCP encapsulation transport; ike-tcp-service and ike-tls-service are per-VDOM gates; TLS mode is FortiGate-to-FortiGate.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IKEv2 begins over UDP; with TCP/TLS services enabled and transport Auto, the initiator can retry over TCP/TLS; IKE and ESP are carried inside TLS; peer certificate validation precedes Phase 2 and normal firewall-policy traffic.
topics.failure_class: UDP blocked but fallback disabled; TLS listener disabled on one peer; untrusted or mismatched certificate; FortiClient incorrectly expected to use the new FortiGate-to-FortiGate TLS mode; post-upgrade static Auto tunnel conversion misunderstood.
topics.evidence_pattern: IKE gateway output identifies transport and peer; IKE debug shows TLS handshake/certificate result; packet capture shows TCP/TLS; established SA does not prove routes or firewall policies pass application traffic.
topics.remediation_path: Enable TCP/TLS services on both peers; use IKEv2 and Auto; import correct CA and use matching peer identity; validate listener/port, route and policy separately; review upgrade conversion; do not conflate RFC8229 TCP encapsulation with the new TLS mode.
topics.question_fingerprint: separate UDP negotiation, TCP fallback gates, TLS certificate validation and post-tunnel policy failure from their distinct evidence.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: two FortiGates, UDP-first path, TCP/TLS 1.3 fallback, mutual peer trust, IKE/ESP encapsulation and separate protected-data policy path.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 ADOM upgrade readiness: syntax compatibility, database conversion and remote-certificate preflight
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: ADOM version is the FortiOS syntax/database schema version, not FortiManager firmware; readiness checks device configurations for unsupported syntax before ADOM object conversion and reports blockers without repairing them.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select same-version ADOMs; readiness evaluates device/VDOM syntax; exported report drives remediation; ADOM upgrade converts schema/objects; device resync and install preview validate the resulting target syntax.
topics.failure_class: Unsupported device firmware or syntax; malformed remote certificate PEM wrapper; mixed ADOM versions assumed compatible; workspace ADOM not locked; object conversion succeeds but later install exposes a device-specific syntax issue.
topics.evidence_pattern: Readiness report identifies exact incompatible objects; ADOM support matrix establishes version compatibility; Remote Certificate and Where Used reveal SAML/PKI dependencies; successful readiness does not guarantee install success.
topics.remediation_path: Back up FortiManager; verify lowest device firmware; lock workspace ADOM; run readiness; repair invalid syntax and PEM delimiters without changing certificate bytes; upgrade supported ADOM versions together; resync devices and run install preview before production install.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish FortiManager firmware, ADOM schema, managed-device firmware and malformed shared certificate data.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager above multiple ADOM schema lanes; device/VDOM syntax checks feed readiness report; remediation gate precedes schema conversion and device resync/install.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 FortiMQ connector: ADOM-scoped indicator delivery and Cloud Fabric Feed enforcement
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 FortiMQ connector is a disabled-by-default cloud connector that transmits blocked IP, URL, domain or MAC indicators through block_indicator playbook; FortiGate retrieves them as Cloud-based Fabric Feeds; connector scope follows source ADOM.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Logs reach FortiAnalyzer; analyst blocks an indicator; playbook posts to FortiMQ; FortiGate syncs cloud feed; feed object is referenced by a firewall/security profile; unblock reverses indicator state.
topics.failure_class: Connector disabled; FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer not under same FortiCare account; feed sync disabled; ADOM mismatch; indicator submission mistaken for enforcement; existing FortiManager connector assumed to supersede FortiMQ.
topics.evidence_pattern: Active connector proves API health; playbook run proves submission; FortiGate feed contents/last-update prove retrieval; policy/profile reference and traffic test prove enforcement.
topics.remediation_path: Enable connector in the correct Fabric/FortiGate ADOM; confirm same FortiCare account and FortiGate cloud-feed sync; validate indicator type and scope; inspect playbook; confirm feed population and policy reference; disable FortiMQ only when deliberately using the FortiManager path.
topics.question_fingerprint: separate connector health, ADOM scope, indicator submission, feed retrieval and actual policy enforcement.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate logs to FortiAnalyzer ADOM; analyst indicator to playbook to FortiMQ cloud; FortiGate feed sync to external-feed object to policy.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch egress QoS: CoS/DSCP trust maps, eight queues, scheduler weights and congestion drops
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch maps ingress 802.1p CoS or IP DSCP into one of eight egress queues; trust selection determines classification; strict, round-robin and weighted scheduling govern service; tail-drop and model-dependent RED/WRED control congestion.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress trust selects CoS or DSCP map; classification selects queue; optional ACL remarking changes markings; egress policy selects scheduling and rate/drop behavior; policy binds to ports; scheduler transmits or drops under congestion.
topics.failure_class: Wrong trust map selects default queue; both CoS and DSCP trust cause DSCP precedence; queue 7 oversubscribed by data; strict scheduling starves lower queues; model lacks configured min-rate/WRED/ECN options.
topics.evidence_pattern: dot1p/dscp maps and port QoS policy show intent; switch QoS counters show queue occupancy/drop behavior; compare ingress markings and selected queue under controlled congestion; CPU internal queues are not identical to port queue counters.
topics.remediation_path: Choose one trust source per port; map DSCP/CoS intentionally; reserve queue 7 for control; use WRR where starvation is unacceptable; verify model feature matrix; inspect per-port queue counters before tuning.
topics.question_fingerprint: trace voice/data packet classification to egress queue and scheduler while distinguishing port queue 7 from CPU control queues.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: ingress CoS/DSCP trust -> eight egress queues -> strict/RR/WRR scheduler -> tail-drop/WRED/ECN congestion branch -> egress.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiAP 8.0 wireless packet sniffer: radio-channel capture, frame filters and browser-streamed PCAP
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A FortiAP profile places one radio in packet-sniffer mode; captures over-the-air management, control and data frames on a selected channel/channel width with optional station-MAC and frame-type filters; FortiGate GUI streams capture to browser and does not persist PCAP on FortiGate.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select radio in WTP profile; configure sniffer mode/channel/width/buffer/MAC/frame filters; apply profile; start one AP capture; packets stream to browser; stop and save PCAP locally; analyze 802.11 management/control/data frames.
topics.failure_class: Wrong radio/channel/width misses frames; filter excludes target; one AP capture already running; operator changes radio mode before exporting temporary capture; browser stream mistaken for FortiGate-stored PCAP.
topics.evidence_pattern: Profile shows capture settings; AP status confirms radio mode; live stream and saved PCAP expose beacon/probe/control/data, retries, rate and RSSI; no frames proves only that the configured radio/filter/channel did not observe them.
topics.remediation_path: Match channel and width to affected BSS; use separate APs for simultaneous band captures; begin with broad filters; run one capture at a time; save PCAP before changing radio mode; use separate CAPWAP capture when controller transport is suspect.
topics.question_fingerprint: choose over-the-air radio capture versus CAPWAP transport capture and identify where the PCAP is stored.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP radio/channel/filter boundary -> live browser stream -> local PCAP analyzer; separate CAPWAP control/data path.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 MDM service connectors: host registration, health state and polling fan-out
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 MDM Service Connector uses vendor API inventory and health data to register/refresh hosts; optional on-demand registration, automatic inventory polling, application inventory, health revalidation, deletion reconciliation and Manager fan-out are distinct controls.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Unknown host reaches captive portal -> on-demand MDM lookup -> host registration; scheduled poll -> API authentication -> host inventory/health update -> host database -> NAC policy; FortiNAC Manager may poll once and distribute records to managed servers.
topics.failure_class: Stale Last Successful Poll; delegated/application permission mismatch; unsupported proxy path; host identity mismatch; on-demand registration disabled; aggressive health/application polling throttles MDM; Remove Hosts deletes still-needed host records.
topics.evidence_pattern: Last Poll versus Last Successful Poll; Test Connection; Poll Now; service-connector audit log; MDM-managed host record and health fields; Manager propagation to the server controlling the port. A successful connection test does not prove host registration or policy enforcement.
topics.remediation_path: Use application permissions where supported; validate Request URL, application ID, secret/certificate and vendor API permissions; account for no-proxy constraint; enable on-demand registration for unknown hosts; use measured poll intervals; test Remove Hosts in staging; place connector on Manager for shared fan-out or individual servers for selective scope.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish unknown-host on-demand registration, inventory polling, per-connect health revalidation, application inventory and Manager fan-out; interpret Last Poll versus Last Successful Poll.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint/captive portal with on-demand lookup branch; MDM API and scheduled inventory poll; host database/health state; optional Manager fan-out; NAC policy boundary.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 vulnerability-scanner integration: scan thresholds to network enforcement
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 service connectors poll Tenable or Qualys for completed vulnerability scan results; per-scan severity thresholds drive host pass/fail events and optional Host Security actions.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Scanner executes scan -> FortiNAC-F connector polls vendor API -> completed results are matched to target host -> threshold evaluation -> Vulnerability Scan Passed/Failed or integration event -> alarm mapping/Admin Scan -> At Risk/Safe and remediation portal; exception group bypasses normal access enforcement.
topics.failure_class: Scanner not run; target IP absent from Qualys Asset Address Management; API connection failure; concurrent/periodic API limit; threshold misconfigured; scan result skipped/incomplete; exception group masks failure in Host View.
topics.evidence_pattern: Test Connection proves API path only; Poll and vendor scan history prove result availability; Last Vulnerability Scan/Status/Details/Source show processed host result; distinct events identify incomplete, skipped, refused, connection, and rate-limit boundaries.
topics.remediation_path: Validate vendor URL and credentials; run the scan at the vendor; include Qualys target IP in Asset Address Management; poll after completion; tune repetition rate to API limits; validate thresholds and alarm mappings; inspect exception group before treating Passed as a clean scan.
topics.question_fingerprint: differentiate connector health from scan execution/result ingestion; interpret Qualys asset refusal and API limits; map failed/passed events to At Risk/Safe; identify exception-group override.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Tenable/Qualys scanner -> FortiNAC-F API connector/poll -> scan threshold evaluation -> events/alarm mapping -> host risk/remediation; exception bypass branch.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 REST API bulk local-user operations and request correlation
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 REST API adds collection-level POST/DELETE for multiple local users, a users listing field, custom1/custom2/custom3 filters, expanded CSV filters and optional X-Request-ID correlation across read/write operations.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Automation authenticates with dedicated API admin/key over HTTPS -> submits localusers collection request with unique X-Request-ID -> FAC processes request -> response metadata echoes request_id -> GET/filter read-after-write verifies cohort -> downstream RADIUS/group/certificate bindings are validated separately.
topics.failure_class: Ambiguous timeout followed by unsafe duplicate POST/DELETE; malformed/oversized request ID; API key or API-admin permission failure; bulk user operation succeeds but attributes/group bindings are wrong; separate CSV import clears RADIUS certificate binding.
topics.evidence_pattern: HTTP response and meta.request_id; GET /localusers/ objects filtered by custom fields; API/server log correlation; Local Users record, group and RADIUS attribute/certificate-binding checks; Access-Accept confirms downstream authorization. Request ID is correlation, not idempotency or authentication.
topics.remediation_path: Use dedicated API admin and TLS certificate validation; assign a unique <=64-character ASCII request ID; use version-matched batch schema; export/record target cohort; read after write before retry; verify user state, group, RADIUS attributes and certificate binding; treat CSV import as a separate operation.
topics.question_fingerprint: select collection-level POST/DELETE; identify X-Request-ID constraints and echoed response metadata; distinguish CSV import defect from REST batch behavior; verify user state and downstream RADIUS authorization.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Automation client -> API admin/key and HTTPS -> localusers collection batch operation -> response meta/request ID and server logs; GET custom-field read-after-write -> separate RADIUS/group validation.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 JIT privilege via secret checkout/check-in: WinRM PowerShell elevation and de-elevation
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 attaches PowerShell checkout/check-in scripts to a secret; resolves privileged target account; connects over WinRM; adds user to elevated group at checkout and removes at check-in; script failure warns but does not block checkout/check-in.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User checks out secret; FortiPAM resolves target admin credential; WinRM executes Add-LocalGroupMember/Add-ADGroupMember; user signs out/in to refresh token; work proceeds; check-in executes removal script; user signs out/in again.
topics.failure_class: WinRM disabled/unreachable; privileged credential lacks rights; script/identity variable incorrect; script failure while checkout continues; token not refreshed after membership change; check-in skipped.
topics.evidence_pattern: Secret activity shows script result; WinRM service/listener prove reachability; local/AD group membership proves privilege; current logon token may not reflect membership until new logon; checkout alone does not prove elevation.
topics.remediation_path: Enable WinRM and verify service; test scripts; ensure privileged account has minimum group rights; inspect activity logs and membership; force sign-out/in after both transitions; monitor overdue checkouts and failed check-ins.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish script execution from token refresh and explain why checkout may succeed while JIT elevation failed.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM checkout -> credential resolver -> WinRM PowerShell add-group -> new logon token -> check-in remove-group -> refreshed least-privilege token.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Supervisor HA CMDB replication: Patroni timeline divergence, stale PostgreSQL replicas and safe reinitialization
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM Supervisor HA uses PostgreSQL Patroni for CMDB replication and etcd for leader election; failover changes timeline; replica on incompatible timeline can remain running/read-only but stop streaming and leave CMDB stale.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Leader writes CMDB WAL; Patroni streams WAL to replicas; failover elects new leader and advances timeline; valid replicas follow; divergent replica stops applying WAL; detect via Patroni/pg_stat_replication/history; reinitialize only affected replica from healthy leader.
topics.failure_class: Replica running but not streaming after timeline change; health replication widget appears Normal; stale CMDB shows deleted devices/collectors; rebuilding from wrong node or without healthy leader risks data loss.
topics.evidence_pattern: patronictl list shows role/state/TL/lag; patronictl history shows timeline; pg_stat_replication shows streaming; pg_is_in_recovery identifies replica; compare ph_device counts and phshowVersion.sh; WAL timeline errors show divergence.
topics.remediation_path: Confirm healthy leader and streaming replica with lag 0; inspect timeline/history; run patronictl reinit only on affected replica, never leader; monitor same timeline/streaming/lag 0; restart phxctl services; if reinit fails collect Patroni/PostgreSQL logs and stop retrying.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish running from streaming replica and identify safe target/preconditions for Patroni reinit.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: three Supervisor nodes with PostgreSQL Patroni leader/WAL stream; failover timeline branch; stale replica isolated and reinitialized from healthy leader.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiSASE regional compliance geofencing: DNS-based source location, ordered tunnel selection and health-check failover
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE determines remote-user country/region from public-IP/DNS location context, applies Regional access allow/deny, selects matching Regional compliance rule and ordered on-prem/PoP connections; on-prem gateways are ICMP health-checked every 1-2 minutes and DNS failover uses 300-second TTL.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiClient resolves turbo FQDN via recursive DNS; FortiSASE determines region; geofencing gate runs; regional rule selects ordered connections; FortiClient attempts priority list; failed on-prem gateway health check updates DNS to next target; endpoint retries after cache expiry.
topics.failure_class: Recursive resolver is outside user's country; eDNS client-subnet absent; regional-access gate blocks before rule; fallback PoP omitted; on-prem gateway blocks ICMP; DNS cache delays failover.
topics.evidence_pattern: nslookup turbo FQDN shows PoP hostname; nslookup whoami.akamai.com identifies recursive resolver egress; TXT eDNS query reveals client subnet; ICMP and 300-second TTL explain 3-8 minute failover; portal configuration success does not prove resolver-based location.
topics.remediation_path: Use in-country recursive resolver and eDNS client-subnet; compare resolver egress to endpoint; check Regional access before rule; order permitted connections and include fallback PoP; permit ICMP to on-prem gateway; allow for DNS TTL.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish endpoint public IP from recursive resolver location and explain unexpected PoP selection despite a valid regional rule.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: remote endpoint -> recursive DNS/eDNS location -> geofencing gate -> regional priority list -> PoP/on-prem tunnel candidates with ICMP/DNS failover.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN speed-test scheduling: backend coordination and interface bandwidth-bound result shaping
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 coordinates scheduled SD-WAN speed tests between FortiGate and backend; explicit retry/retry-pause settings removed; test traffic bypasses interface shaping but uses update-inbandwidth/outbandwidth min/max values; result-to-interface-shaping settings moved to interface configuration.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure system speed-test-schedule per interface with bounds; FortiGate/backend coordinate test timing; test measures bandwidth; min/max clamp results; interface consumes updated bandwidth values for shaping.
topics.failure_class: Obsolete retry commands carried forward; operator expects interface shaper to govern speed-test packets; result settings left in old location; min/max bounds mistaken for measured values.
topics.evidence_pattern: show system speed-test-schedule displays interface schedule/bounds; 8.0 CLI no longer exposes retry/retry-pause; compare raw and bounded results and interface shaping settings; completed test does not prove application traffic shaping.
topics.remediation_path: Use 8.0 interface-based settings; remove retry/retry-pause assumptions; set min/max bounds intentionally; verify backend coordination and per-interface schedule; test speed-test traffic separately from ordinary shaped traffic.
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish backend retry coordination, bypassed interface shaping and min/max result clamping.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: interface schedule -> backend coordination -> speed-test measurement -> min/max clamp -> shaping consumer; test packets bypass interface shaper.
